requirements.text: I run it with one thing, the folder name. For each dead link it prints the file, the line number, and what the link was pointing at. It exits with an error status if there are any. If there are none it prints one plain line saying so.
requirements.test: Run it on the test folder with known dead links and see file:line and target for each one. Run it on a clean folder and see the single 'no dead links' line and a zero exit.

requirements.text: A link to a note in another folder, or to a note that was renamed and linked under the new name, is not reported when the note exists. It looks through the whole folder tree, not just the same folder.
requirements.test: In the test folder, a note in a nested subfolder is linked from a note in the top folder and from a note in a different subfolder. Neither link appears in the output.

requirements.text: A link to a heading inside a note is checked against the hash-sign headings actually in that note. A heading that is there is not reported. A heading that isn't there is reported.
requirements.test: The test folder has one link to a heading that exists and one to a heading that doesn't. Only the second is printed.

requirements.text: A link to a note that doesn't exist yet, like my Rings note pointing at a family note I haven't written, is reported every run, in the same words each time. There is no way to silence it.
requirements.test: The test folder has a note linking to a missing note. It appears in the output on two runs in a row, identical.

requirements.text: If a link could match more than one note (same name in two folders), the tool says that plainly, naming both files, instead of choosing one and calling the link good or broken.
requirements.test: The test folder has two notes with the same name in different folders and a link to that name. The output names both files for that link.

requirements.text: At the end of a run, if any lines contain a plain-words 'see ...' that isn't a proper link, it prints one line saying how many such lines were not checked. Those lines are never reported as dead.
requirements.test: Put 'see Shoes' and 'see you Tuesday' in plain text in a test note; run it; neither is reported as dead, and the closing line says 2 lines were not checked.

requirements.text: The tool is one file called linkcheck.py, with its tests in test_linkcheck.py, and I run it as python3 linkcheck.py FOLDER.
requirements.test: ls shows linkcheck.py and test_linkcheck.py and no deadlinks.py; python3 linkcheck.py test_notes prints the same dead links as before.

requirements.text: A link to a heading whose title has other marks in it (a link, bold, or trailing hash signs) is matched on the plain words of the heading. If the words are there, it is not reported.
requirements.test: A demo note with a heading like '## See [Shoes](Shoes.md)' or '## Rings ##' and a link to it. Run it. The link is not reported. A link to a wrong heading in the same note still is.
